html:
The Democratic Party's sweeping victory in the US midterm elections, securing full control of Congress, marks the day's most significant global development, with Donald Trump acknowledging the ongoing war in Iran as a key factor in Republican defeats. This outcome is poised to reshape US foreign and domestic policy and has already influenced global markets.

US Politics & Global Impact: Democrats achieved historic victories, winning control of both the House and Senate, a reversal from Republican control since 2023. Wall Street surged on the news, with the Dow Jones rising 2%. The Republican Party has begun a blame game, with Vance offering a scathing election critique blaming the Iran war, a sharp break with Trump who, in turn, admitted the war's role in the defeat, though asserting it was worthwhile. Elon Musk's record spending of nearly half a billion dollars backing Republican candidates proved a flop. Michigan's first Muslim senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed, made history, among other Arab and Muslim candidates achieving historic wins.

US-Iran & Middle East Security: The "Iran war" remains a central point of global contention. Donald Trump confirmed US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, stating, "We watched it get built — then we hit it." Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, stated Americans voted "no to war," a message he endorsed, while Iran's supreme leader asserted that US hostility would persist regardless of election results. South Korea, under pressure from Trump, plans to expand its anti-piracy Cheonghae unit's operations closer to the Strait of Hormuz to keep the waterway open, but ruled out military intervention in the ongoing US-Iran war. Trump also announced the US would end $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel starting in 2027, a plan welcomed by Abdul El-Sayed. Israel reportedly warned the US that Iran is considering using chemical weapons. Meanwhile, Israel’s Herzog accepted vote results, dealing a blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's efforts to discredit the elections after his party and allies lost their majority.

Russia-Ukraine & Broader Security: Ukraine reported a deadly Russian "double-tap bombing" on a village, with at least 40 killed and dozens more missing, according to Kyiv and President Zelenskyy, who said 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles, and 59 cruise missiles were launched. A short ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region briefly allowed residents a return to normal life. In other security developments, North Korea reportedly tested a ballistic missile with a cluster warhead and a strategic cruise missile. China's foreign minister stated a commitment to deepening ties between China and North Korea.

Hong Kong & China: Joshua Wong, a prominent figure in Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, was sentenced to 10 more years in prison for "foreign collusion," his second conviction under the controversial national security law, bringing his total imprisonment to nearly six years. This sentencing adds to concerns over the erosion of political freedoms in the city. Separately, Canada and China extended a tariff deal, aiming to boost Canadian exports. Chinese AI chatbots are reportedly censoring controversy around footballer Kylian Mbappé's comments on Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Global Economy & Other Events: Beyond the US midterms' market impact, Australia’s upmarket department store David Jones collapsed into voluntary administration after years of losses, putting thousands of jobs at risk. East Asia has been battered by unusually wild typhoons, with the Pacific described as "burning with fever" due to El Niño. In the Indian Ocean, the Indian navy rescued 20 crew from an Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia, following a resurgence of piracy. Hungary is opening its Communist-era secret service files 36 years later, sparking new debates. Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese diplomats amid accusations of allowing the paramilitary RSF to launch drone strikes from its territory.
